title: Isaiah 53 foretold the Messiah’s passion for us
source_text: X. Qua de re multis ante Christi adventum saeculis clare admodum fuit vaticinatus Isaias, cap. 53. ubi juxta morem propheticum, de rebus futuris verbis praeteriti temporis loquens, sic venturi Messiae passiones pro nobis describit. Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, & dolores nostros portavit; nos autem reputavimus eum plagis afflictum, percussum & humiliatum a Deo. Ipse autem vulneratus est propter praevaricationes nostras, attritus est propter iniquitates nostras: castigatio pacis nostrae super eum, & livore ejus sanati sumus. Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus, unusquisque in viam suam declinavit; & posuit Dominus in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Et postea, Propter praevaricationem populi mei plaga fuit ei. Item, Effudit in mortem animam suam, & cum praevaricatoribus annumeratus est, ipseque peccatum multorum tulit, & pro peccatoribus oravit.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning this Isaiah prophesied very clearly many ages before Christ’s coming, chapter 53, where according to prophetic custom, speaking of future things in past-tense words, he thus describes the coming Messiah’s sufferings for us: Truly he himself bore our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we esteemed him stricken, smitten and humbled by God. But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruise we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, each turned to his own way; and the Lord laid on him the iniquity of us all. And afterward: For the transgression of my people he was stricken. Likewise: He poured out his soul unto death, and was numbered with transgressors, and he bore the sin of many, and prayed for sinners.
pass_b_english: Isaiah 53, speaking future as past, depicts the Messiah bearing our griefs and iniquity.
Wounded for our transgressions; by his bruise we are healed; soul poured out for many.
